task_text: NDT Inspection: The hovering aerial manipulator starts outside a large warehouse building, facing one of its long walls, and high up on that wall a small rectangle is marked out with yellow-and-black hazard tape. Carry out a non-destructive-testing style inspection: bring the end effector to the fixed inspection point in front of the marked rectangle (see the goal geometry) and keep it there for 100 consecutive control steps (0.83 s). Success: With e the position of ee_link's origin (not the tool tip) and g = (1.77, 0.0, 7.0) m (goal_position; environment origin = world origin), a control step is 'in' when |e_x - g_x| < 0.03 m and sqrt((e_y - g_y)^2 + (e_z - g_z)^2) < 0.08 m. A counter increases by 1 at every 'in' step and is reset to 0 at every step that is not; success when it reaches 100 (success_hold_steps), i.e. at the 100th consecutive 'in' step (100/120 s, about 0.83 s). Orientation, velocity and contact are not tested. g is 0.192 m in front of the marker's origin, so with ee_link level and pointing at the wall the tool-tip point is about 2 cm short of the wall surface. AM-Bench reports inspection_target_held (the success itself) as its only criterion. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; the 100-step hold above is the only hold requirement. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 20 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 2400 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 2399th step. Goal geometry: The inspection point is fixed, the same in every instance, and not itself marked in the scene: g = (1.77, 0.0, 7.0) m in world coordinates (z up; the robot starts with base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) facing +x). The success region for ee_link's origin is |x - 1.77| < 0.03 m and sqrt(y^2 + (z - 7.0)^2) < 0.08 m. It lies on the robot's side of the taped rectangle, opposite its centre, a little less than 20 cm from it.
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where AM-Bench's success check holds, when the task's episode length of 20 s of simulated time runs out (AM-Bench's time-out, at control step 2399), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
